simple.meaning: מִרְיָם (Miryâm) appears 15 times in the Hebrew Scriptures and is introduced as a sister in the family line and in connection with prophetic witness.
simple.biblicalBackground: The first appearances are in Exodus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, 1 Chronicles, Micah, beginning at Exodus 15:20. BibleIQ detects the main surrounding context as family, death, prophetic witness, wilderness, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מִרְיָם (H4813) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: People in Scripture are understood by their place in the story. BibleIQ follows מִרְיָם through the actual verses so the reader sees the person in context instead of as an isolated dictionary entry.
simple.summary: מִרְיָם (Miryâm) / H4813 is tracked through Exodus 15:20, Exodus 15:21, Numbers 12:1, Numbers 12:4. The entry is generated from source alignment, occurrence evidence, and the surrounding Scripture context.

timeline.evidenceText: Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took a tambourine in her hand; and all the women went out after her with tambourines and with dances.
Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses because of the Cushite woman whom he had married; for he had married a Cushite woman.
Yahweh spoke suddenly to Moses, to Aaron, and to Miriam, “You three come out to the Tent of Meeting!”
Yahweh came down in a pillar of cloud, and stood at the door of the Tent, and called Aaron and Miriam; and they both came forward.
The cloud departed from over the Tent; and behold, Miriam was leprous, as white as snow. Aaron looked at Miriam, and behold, she was leprous.
The cloud departed from over the Tent; and behold, Miriam was leprous, as white as snow. Aaron looked at Miriam, and behold, she was leprous.
Miriam was shut up outside of the camp seven days, and the people didn’t travel until Miriam was brought in again.
Miriam was shut up outside of the camp seven days, and the people didn’t travel until Miriam was brought in again.
The children of Israel, even the whole congregation, came into the wilderness of Zin in the first month. The people stayed in Kadesh. Miriam died there, and was buried there.
The name of Amram’s wife was Jochebed, the daughter of Levi, who was born to Levi in Egypt. She bore to Amram Aaron and Moses, and Miriam their sister.
Remember what Yahweh your God did to Miriam, by the way as you came out of Egypt.
The sons of Ezrah: Jether, Mered, Epher, and Jalon; and she bore Miriam, Shammai, and Ishbah the father of Eshtemoa.
For I brought you up out of the land of Egypt,

definitions.short: Mirjam , the name of two Israelitesses
definitions.full: H4813. Miryam מִרְיָם proper name, feminine and masculine 1. feminine sister of Aaron Exod 15:20 (E), and of Moses and Aaron Num 26:59 (P), 1 Chronicles 5:29; named also Exod 15:21 (E), Num 12:1 , 4 , 5 , 10 (twice in verse); 12:15 (twice in verse); 20:1 (all J E), Deut 24:9 ; Micah 6:4 . ᵐ5 Μαριαμ . 2. masculine (probably) a Judahite 1Chr 4:17 . ᵐ5 τὸν Μαιων , ᵐ5 L Μωεωρ . מְרִירִי מְרִירוּת, see מרר . מֹ֫רֶךְ see רכך . מֶרְכָּבָה מֶרְכָּב, see רכב . [ מַרְכֹּ֫לֶת see רכל . I. מִרְמָה see רמה .
